RE: SALEM Spirit Black Campaign
Kool & The Gang Promotion Offer

Dear Ken:

As you know, the Brand will execute a "B2G1F" coupon offer on the backcover of the Kool & The Gang concert playbill, and while recognizing that this is being viewed as an opportunity to "test" this solicitation vehicle, I feel that the normal "results analysis" should be conducted to assess the Brand's payback on investment. This will require an accurate concert playbill distribution figure against the total venues which should be requested by RJR Media through Elliot Lobel.
I also believe that it might be worthwhile to attend some of the Kool & The Gang concerts, Brand/Agency schedules permitting, to have "hands-on" experience with the Black music scene that could be additive to our current knowledge. Again, I feel that Elliot Lobel should be contacted for free tickets, and the Brand should request samples of all collateral materials for review.

Additionally, depending on the SALEM Brand Team's assessment of Kool & The Gang, we may elect to pursue this group to communicate the Brand's "platform for sociability" in the 1985 Black Street Scenes program.

50222 8308

Let's discuss these thoughts at your earliest convenience.

Sincerely yours,

[SIGNATURE] Philip K. Brown
